citation.authors: Violi F, Loffredo L, Pignatelli P, et al.
citation.title: Extra virgin olive oil use is associated with improved post-prandial blood glucose and LDL cholesterol in healthy subjects

reported.what: glucose, before and 2 h after the lunch with 10 g EVOO vs 10 g corn oil, n=25; the +/- is not labelled in the table
the pre-lunch (1300 h) values of the healthy group, same unlabelled +/-; not a fasting sample (the paper does not say what was eaten before)

location.quote: a blood sample was taken before (at 1300 hours) and 2 h after the lunch

detail: The tables print mean±spread with no label, and the Methods contradict each other ("means±s.d. unless otherwise indicated" against "results were expressed as means±s.e."), so SD or SEM cannot be told; in addition the lunch's carbohydrate, protein and fat grams are not in the text (only the foods and 894 calories, macros in the Supplementary Data) and the 1300 h pre-lunch sample is not a stated fasting state.
